 ⚽️ Nations League updates from 7.45pm GMT
 ⚽️ Kane sets cap record | Live scoreboard | Email Scott 
 LIVE  Updated  now Scott Murray Thu 12 Nov 2026 15.24 EST First published on Thu 12 Nov 2026 13.00 EST Share Key events 12m ago GOAL! England 1-0 Croatia (Rogers 24) 
 1h ago Tuchel on Kane: 'the full package' 
 2h ago The teams 
 2h ago Preamble 
 Morgan Rogers opens the scoring. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian View image in fullscreen Morgan Rogers opens the scoring. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Scott Murray Thu 12 Nov 2026 15.24 EST First published on Thu 12 Nov 2026 13.00 EST Share Key events 12m ago GOAL! England 1-0 Croatia (Rogers 24) 
 1h ago Tuchel on Kane: 'the full package' 
 2h ago The teams 
 2h ago Preamble 
 now 15.24 EST 37 min: England play some patient stuff in the middle of the park. Thomas Tuchel will be happier to watch this state of affairs than the controller of ITV1.
 Share 2m ago 15.22 EST 35 min: A Croatia free kick out on the left. It’s floated towards Baturina, but Anderson is there to clear. Pickford hasn’t had a serious save to make yet. England counter, Rogers finding Bellingham in the box with a sliderule down the right. Bellingham spins and shoots first time, but there’s no power in this shot either, and Croatia clear their lines.
 Share 5m ago 15.20 EST 33 min: Kovačić looks for the top right from 25 yards. No real power, not enough curl. Easy for Pickford. Meanwhile here’s some much-needed good news for those interested in preserving the legacy of poor old Crazy Horse: “On the plus side,” begins Philip Cornwall, “Emlyn Hughes was the only man to play football for England in all of the 60s, 70s and 80s.”
 Share 7m ago 15.18 EST 31 min: Some Newcastle-flavoured fun as Hall’s long-distance drive is deflected out for a corner, from which Burn batters a headers goalwards. It’s blocked, and perhaps had the ball gone in, Burn would have been penalised for climbing fairly obviously on the back of Mišić. But play goes on, so we’ll never know for sure.
 Share 8m ago 15.17 EST 29 min: Croatia had started confidently, but after conceding that scrappy goal, passes aren’t sticking any more. Vlašić tries to control a cross coming in from the left, but loses the flight, spins around, and the ball hits him on the back and out for a throw. All a bit too slapstick for Slaven Bilic’s liking; the Croatia coach stands on the touchline in a mild huff.
 Share 10m ago 15.15 EST 27 min: Hall sends a free kick into the Croatian mixer from the left. Quansah rises highest at the far stick, but it’s an easy, looping claim for Livaković.
 Share 11m ago 15.14 EST 26 min: Poor Livaković, who had initially gone the wrong way, scrambled to get back towards that, but Rogers had sent it on a weird arc that ensured he couldn’t claw it out. Croatia will feel sick after starting the game pretty well.
 Share 12m ago 15.12 EST GOAL! England 1-0 Croatia (Rogers 24)
 Kane pings another long diagonal. This time left to right for Bellingham, just to the side of the six-yard box. Bellingham cushions it instantly into the centre. The ball goes through the flapping Gvardiol’s legs. Rogers bundles it into the bottom right … so slowly … but the bounce takes it into the net, almost apologetically so.
 View image in fullscreen Morgan Rogers opens the scoring. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Share Updated at  15.24 EST 14m ago 15.10 EST 23 min: Croatia probe down the left. No way through. The ball’s cut back for Mišić, who obviously loses patience with the careful examination and drags a weak shot miles left. Pickford wanders across to see it out, no need to panic about that .
 Share 16m ago 15.08 EST 21 min: The pace drops a bit, and the game turns shapeless. A lot of middle-of-park nonsense I won’t bother you with.
 Share 17m ago 15.07 EST 19 min: The period of play after that rebound ends up with England winning their first corner of the evening. Rice sends it in from the right. Matanović powers a header clear. Alexander-Arnold, deep on the left, floats a diagonal towards Rogers, who tries to tee up Kane with a cutback from the right-hand edge of the six-yard box. Stanišić is on point to hoick clear. England have finally turned up.
 Share 19m ago 15.06 EST 18 min: Bellingham’s cross from the right is only half cleared. Alexander-Arnold shapes like Zidane in the 2002 Champions League final, pearling a drive that’s bravely blocked by Mišić.
 Share 21m ago 15.03 EST 16 min: Gordon and Hall combine well down the left. Rice rolls a cute pass infield for Anderson, who leans back and sends a shot from the edge of the box well over the bar. A corner’s awarded, then snatched back from under England’s nose by VAR.
 Share 22m ago 15.02 EST 15 min: … so having said that, Croatia launch another attack. A simple long ball down the middle nearly does for the centre-back pairing of Quansah and Burn, but when the ball ends up at the feet of Sučić, with space to advance into down the left, the Croatia man hesitates and the opportunity is gone.
 Share 24m ago 15.00 EST 13 min: England take their turn to stroke the ball around. Their first opportunity of the evening. It firmly puts a stop to Croatia’s early gallop.
 Share 26m ago 14.59 EST 11 min: Kane drops deep and finds Hall on the left with a raking long diagonal. Hall’s cross is no good, but what a pass. You think how good Kane is already; imagine what he’s going to be like when he finally enters the autumnal quarterback phase of his career!
 Share 27m ago 14.57 EST 9 min: Croatia continue to hog the ball. They’ve done a good job of quietening the Wembley crowd. It’s their fans making most of the noise. Meanwhile more Emlyn Hughes-infused tutting, this time from our man Philip Cornwall: “Hughes was also in the 1980 Euros squad, but again didn’t play.” I bet Roger Kirkby wishes he never mentioned it now.
 Share 29m ago 14.55 EST 7 min: Vušković is nearly closed down in his own box by a pincer movement launched by Rogers and Gordon. He shuffles his way out of danger elegantly.
 Share 31m ago 14.54 EST 6 min: … again nothing. But this is a really confident start from Croatia , and a reminder that they’re in serious reputation-salvaging mode tonight after England inflicted that record seven-goal defeat on them at home.
 Share 32m ago 14.53 EST 5 min: … nothing much happens. England win a throw. But then the ball’s played back to Pickford, who attempts to drop a shoulder around Matanović, and is fairly lucky the ball only rebounds out for another corner. From which …
 View image in fullscreen England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford (left) and Croatia's Igor Matanovic battle for the ball. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA Share Updated at  15.11 EST 33m ago 14.51 EST 4 min: Vlašić drives hard down the left and wins the evening’s first corner of the evening off Alexander-Arnold. From which …
 Share 34m ago 14.50 EST 2 min: Croatia continue to hog the ball during the early exchanges. “Emlyn Hughes did go to a World Cup, in 1970,” tut-tuts Paul Fields. “He just didn’t win a cap there. He was an unused squad member.”
 Share 36m ago 14.48 EST Croatia get the ball rolling. They’re off to a fast (ish) start, Sučić robbing Hall down the right and cutting back for Kovačić, who sends the ball sky high. Goal kick.
 Share 40m ago 14.44 EST The teams are out! England are in their first-choice white, forcing Croatia out of their famous red-and-white checks and into their alternative kit of blue. A large tifo in the stand to celebrate “England’s finest: Kane 126”. Kane has four special mascots with him: his four children, all with England tops and “Kane 126” on their back. Kane first lifts his Ballon d’Or, then receives a gong from none other than Mr 125, Peter Shilton, who graciously smiles and congratulates his usurper. Luka Modrić then arrives with a replica of a ball taken by English industrialists to Croatia in 1880. And finally here comes the Prince of Wales, to give Harry one of those Kane 126 shirts in a lovely easy-to-hang frame. Kane raises his arms in weary triumph; after dealing with that little lot, he must be knackered already. We’ll be off in a minute!
 Share 49m ago 14.36 EST Pre-match postbag. “With tonight’s record being broken, spare a thought for the holder of a more unwanted record, Emlyn Hughes. He won 62 caps and never got to go to the World Cup or Euros finals” – Roger Kirkby
 “In the non-Kane-focused-Croatian World of Sport, does Modric’s pine-based residency mean he carried the can for that thing that happened last time? Is he now being shown a Ronaldo-shaped door (the other one)? Do Croatians want this? Is there a ‘Modrić van’ waiting for him every time he is picked?” – Ian Copestake
 “Just noticed that if you combine the top 11 of the England appearance list you: (a) get a pretty sensible team, and (b) recreate both England’s traditional left-side problem AND the Gerrard-Lampard conundrum.
 Shilton
Walker/Moore/Wright/Cole
Beckham/Lampard/Gerrard/Charlton
Rooney/Kane 
 Not sure what conclusions to draw from this” – Alex Coldrick-Ford
 Share 1h ago 14.23 EST … meanwhile, as for the new-look central defensive pairing of Jarell Quansah and Dan Burn, Tuchel says … “It is never easy … it is a crucial pairing in the centre of defence … we are forced to do it … normally Marc [Guehi] and Ezri [Konsa] are the ones to have the shirt … John Stones is not with us … so Jarell [Quansah] kept his place from the Czech game and we went 51 percent for Dan Burn because of his experience … and we have Lewis Hall and Anthony Gordon … so we have a bit of a left side from Newcastle … they know each other … they have done it at the highest level in the Champions League.”
 … and finally a word about the goalkeepers, with a trip to Spain at the weekend coming up. “I think we will change [from Jordan Pickford to James Trafford] but let’s see.”
 Share 1h ago 14.18 EST Tuchel on Kane: 'the full package'
 Thomas Tuchel speaks to ITV, who ask him about the secret to record-breaking Harry Kane’s success. “There is no secret … it is hard work … it is personality … it is talent, dedication, focus … the full package … he is not normally the loudest voice in the dressing room, but he is still our leader and our captain … it is not easy what he is doing because he gets a lot of praise and more attention than ever … even attention and praise and compliments can be very draining … hopefully he can brush it off and enjoy the match … enjoy the intensity and be decisive for us.”
 Share 1h ago 14.14 EST Jude and Jobe Bellingham will become the 22nd set of brothers to play for England if Jobe gets off the bench at any point tonight. If Jude remains on the pitch, they’ll be just the 11th to play together for England: only Bobby and Jackie Charlton, and Gary and Phil Neville, have done that since the war. Here is the full list of brothers to have represented England …
 Charlie (1872) and William Clegg (1873-79)
William (1875-77) and Herbert Rawson (1875)
Hubert (1873-78) and Frank Heron (1876)
Alfred (1877) and Ed Lyttelton (1878)
Ernest (1876), Charlie (1879-87) and Arthur Bambridge (1881)
Arthur (1876-83) and Harry Cursham (1880-84)
Fred (1880-82) and Jack Hargreaves (1881)
Arthur (1885-90) and Percy Walters (1885-90)
Alf (1882-84) and Charley Dobson (1886)
Charlie (1888) and Alf Shelton (1889-92)
Robert (1893-94) and Arthur Topham (1894)
Charlie (1890-93) and Tom Perry (1898)
Frank (1898-1903) and Fred Forman (1899)
Charles (1889) and Geoffrey Wilson (1900)
Bertie (1901) and Rex Corbett (1903)
Frank (1922-1926) and Reg Osbourne (1927)
Clem (1924) and George Stephenson (1928-1931)
Jack (1931) and Sep Smith (1935)
Bobby (1958-1970) and Jack Charlton (1965-1970)
Gary (1995-2007) and Phil Neville (1996-2007)
Nathaniel (2018) and Trevoh Chalobah (2025) 
 Share 1h ago 14.10 EST Kane’s record breaking cap is being celebrated in a number of ways at Wembley.
 View image in fullscreen Harry Kane’s shirt inside the England dressing room. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A scarf featuring England captain Harry Kane. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA View image in fullscreen A Harry Kane 126 England strip in the shop. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA View image in fullscreen England and Harry Kane stickers are seen on a seat number 126. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty Images Share Updated at  14.11 EST 1h ago 13.59 EST From the archive … here’s how the Guardian reported on Peter Shilton’s final cap for England . Harry Kane knocks him off the top of England’s all-time appearance list tonight. Shilton has been there since 7 June 1989, when he earned his 109th cap against Denmark in Copenhagen, besting Bobby Moore’s total in doing so. All things must pass, and a 37-year reign isn’t bad going.
 Archive, 1990: Peter Shilton wins 125th and final cap of record-breaking England career Read more Share 2h ago 13.51 EST Croatia start with some familiar faces in their line-up: Manchester City duo Mateo Kovačić and Joško Gvardiol, Brighton defender Luka Vušković, and erstwhile Everton and West Ham striker Nikola Vlašić. Luka Modrić, who suddenly looked all of his 41 years during last month’s seven-goal hammering, is relegated to the bench, but will earn his 207th cap if he gets on tonight.
 Thomas Tuchel keeps laser focus on ‘unfinished business’ with England Read more Share 2h ago 13.40 EST The headline news is obviously Jordan Pickford’s 93rd cap Harry Kane’s record-breaking 126th appearance for England . Thomas Tuchel makes three changes to the side that started the 3-0 win over Czechia: Dan Burn, Declan Rice and Anthony Gordon come in for Marc Guéhi, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Eberechi Eze. For the record, Pickford will still need another 32 caps if he’s to equal Peter Shilton’s all-time goalkeeping total for England.
 Harry Kane’s England caps record: an illustrious career in numbers and charts Read more Share 2h ago 13.32 EST The teams
 England: Pickford, Alexander-Arnold, Quansah, Burn, Hall, Rice, Anderson, Jude Bellingham, Gordon, Kane, Rogers.
 Subs: Trafford, Steele, Gibbs-White, White, Hill, Branthwaite, Jobe Bellingham, Garner, Calvert-Lewin, Ngumoha, Eze, King. 
 Croatia: Livakovic, Stanisic, Vuskovic, Gvardiol, Kovacic, Vlasic, Smolcic, Baturina, Sucic, Matanovic, Misic.
 Subs: Pandur, Kotarski, Caleta-Car, Galesic, Majer, Beljo, Modric, Budimir, Mario Psaslic, Hrgovic, Marco Pasalic, Soticek. 
 Referee: Morten Krogh (Denmark) 
 Share Updated at  13.42 EST 2h ago 13.00 EST Preamble
 A whopping 40 days ago, this happened … 
 Croatia 0-7 England: Nations League football – as it happened Read more … and while Croatia will be desperate to summon some sort of face-saving, reputation-salvaging, self-respect-restoring response tonight, they’d do well to consider that: (a) it’s not very likely, if their defenders again randomly skitter around like they did in Rijeka; (b) it’d almost certainly make not a jot of difference to their borderline-non-existent hopes of making the quarters † , and; (c) hey, they’ve always got the Euro 2008 qualifiers and the 2018 World Cup semi to keep them warm at night. So in that three-part sense, this is a bit of a non-event, though tell that to Harry Kane, who will break the all-time appearance record for the Three Lions ‡ . Kick-off at Wembley is at 7.45pm GMT. It, almost exclusively for England, is on!
 †: After the first four matches in Group A3, the table looks like this …
 1. Spain P4 GD+7 Pts 12
2. England P4 GD+11 Pts 9 
3. Croatia P4 GD-10 Pts 3
4. Czechia P4 GD-8 Pts 0 
 … which means Spain are definitely through. England are as well, if we’re all being honest with each other. They can only be pipped by Croatia if they lose both of their final two matches in this November break (tonight’s game, then away on Sunday night to Spain) while Croatia win both of theirs (this one, then their hosting of Czechia ) and even then, because things would go to the head-to-head, Croatia would have to beat England tonight by a minimum of seven goals.
 ‡: The all-time England men’s appearance list …
 125: Peter Shilton, Harry Kane
120: Wayne Rooney
115: David Beckham
114: Steven Gerrard
108: Bobby Moore
107: Ashley Cole
106: Bobby Charlton, Frank Lampard
105: Billy Wright
96: Kyle Walker
94: John Stones
92: Jordan Pickford
91: Jordan Henderson
90: Bryan Robson
